This week: ubiquitous and tangible computing

When the computer disappears, who checks its work?

Mark Weiser · 1991

“The most profound technologies are those that disappear. They weave themselves into the fabric of everyday life until they are indistinguishable from it.”[1]

Hiroshi Ishii & Brygg Ullmer · 1997

Tangible Bits: “grasp & manipulate” bits at the center of attention, and sense “background bits at the periphery of human perception.”[2]

A voice prompt and an agent are interfaces that disappear: no screen, no menu, sometimes no keyboard. Today is about what that does to checking the result.

CARC · UNM · CS 491/591 Intro to HCI · Nov. 13, 2026
The thread through this talk

How we ask questions of data is changing

Query

Write SQL or click filters. You must already know where the data is and what it is called.

→

Search

Type keywords. An engine ranks documents; you still read them and do the analysis.

→

Ask

Type or say a question. A language model answers from what it read in training.

→

Delegate

State a goal. An agent finds the data through its metadata, follows a knowledge graph, runs trained models, checks the result, and reports.

The deeper the question, the more the answer rests on metadata, knowledge graphs, and models trained by machine learning and reinforcement learning, and on how well you say what you mean, by voice or keyboard.

Norman’s gulfs, and a third for language models

AI shrinks one gulf and widens another

Envisioning · 2024

Before you ask

Can it do this? How should I say it? How will I judge the answer?[3]

Execution · 1985

Goal → system

Once a menu, a syntax, a manual[4]. Now one sentence, typed or spoken. The syntax is gone; the articulation is not.

Evaluation · 1985

System → goal

Forty changed files, tests you did not write, a confident summary. Wider than ever.

Everything in this talk is a tool for crossing the gulf of evaluation.

CARC · UNM · CS 491/591 Intro to HCI · Nov. 13, 2026
Primer · the data side

Six words for asking deeper questions of data

Metadata

“Data about data”: what, who, when, where, in what units[5]. FAIR asks that it be usable by machines, not only people[6].

Ontology

A formal, machine-readable statement of what terms mean[7]: Carabidae, the ground beetles, is a family within Coleoptera, the beetles[8].

Knowledge graph

Things as nodes, relations as edges: specimen → collected at → site[7]. GraphRAG lets a language model answer questions across one[9].

Machine learning

A system learns if its performance at a task improves with experience[10]; supervised models learn from labeled examples to classify, detect or segment.

Reinforcement learning

Learning what to do by trial and error to maximize a reward[11]. It tunes chatbots to follow instructions[12] and trains reasoning and coding agents[13,14].

Agentic AI · harness

A language model using tools in a loop, choosing its next step from what comes back[15]. The harness is the app you talk to: Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity.

Where the term comes from · Feb. 2, 2025

The first vibe coder was talking, not typing

“There’s a new kind of coding I call ‘vibe coding’, where you fully give in to the vibes, embrace exponentials, and forget that the code even exists.”
The same post

“I just talk to Composer with SuperWhisper so I barely even touch the keyboard. … I ‘Accept All’ always, I don’t read the diffs anymore.”

Andrej Karpathy, post on X[31]

Nine months later

Collins Word of the Year 2025: “the use of artificial intelligence prompted by natural language to write computer code.”

Collins Dictionary[32]

The gulf of evaluation, measured

Feeling faster is not being faster

19%

longer to finish real issues with early-2025 AI tools

16 experienced open-source developers, 246 issues. They forecast a 24% speedup, and afterwards still believed in a 20% one[33].

Tools improve fast: by Feb. 2026 METR called its follow-up an unreliable signal, because more developers declined to work without AI[34]. The gap between feeling and measurement is the point.

5.2% and 21.7%

at least, on average: the share of packages in code from commercial and open-source models that did not exist. 205,474 unique invented names in 576,000 samples, each one a name an attacker can register[35].

45%

of cases introduced a security vulnerability, across 80 coding tasks and more than 100 models. A vendor’s own report, not peer reviewed[36].

CARC · UNM · CS 491/591 Intro to HCI · Nov. 13, 2026
A spoken prompt is a brief

Say the context; type the identifiers

TYPED IN A HURRY · 7 WORDS
add time travel to the beetle lake
SPOKEN · 79 WORDS · ILLUSTRATION, NOT DATA
In the beetle seg repo, add a time travel query to the duck lake metadata history, not the measurements. Use the existing client; no new dependencies. Take a collection path and a date, and return the a views as they were on that date. Read only: nothing writes to eye rods. Add a test that uses last week’s snapshot, run the linter, and only then tell me it’s done. If the snapshot has expired, say so instead of guessing.

Check the nouns

Dictation fails on names: DuckLake (data format), AVUs (metadata tags), iRODS (data store). Misheard words are underlined.

Read before Enter

A misheard word becomes an instruction the agent will follow.

Pin down what must be exact

Type, spell out, or add to a custom vocabulary: paths, identifiers, numbers, code.

03

Ethics

Principles, concerns, and who decides.
AI ethics · principles and rules

Many AI principles are interface requirements

Floridi & Cowls · 2019

Five principles for AI in society

Beneficence · Non-maleficence · Autonomy · Justice · Explicability[43]

Explicability, being able to see how a decision was made and who is responsible, is what makes the other four checkable.

White House OSTP · Oct. 2022

Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights

Safe and Effective Systems · Algorithmic Discrimination Protections · Data Privacy · Notice and Explanation · Human Alternatives, Consideration, and Fallback[44]

Non-binding. The two in bold are design requirements: tell people an automated system is in use, and let them reach a person.

HCI is where principles become interfaces: a disclosure, an explanation, a way to reach a human.

CARC · UNM · CS 491/591 Intro to HCI · Nov. 13, 2026
AI ethics · the concerns

Serious questions deserve serious answers

Power and water

Data-centre electricity is projected to more than double by 2030, to about 945 TWh, about what Japan uses today[45]. Cheaper AI may mean more AI, as Jevons saw with coal[46].

Consent and credit

Courts have held training on books to be fair use, but pirated copies went to trial: Bartz v. Anthropic settled for $1.5 billion, about $3,000 per work[47].

Bias

A widely used US care algorithm steered less care to Black patients because it used past health spending as a proxy for need[48].

Accountability

In the July 2026 OpenAI–Hugging Face incident, roughly 7% of agent transcripts carried spoofed tool calls; an independent investigation established what happened[49].

Each could be its own lecture. GPT 101’s ethics module covers them in depth[50].

CARC · UNM · CS 491/591 Intro to HCI · Nov. 13, 2026
AI ethics · the 2026 debate

Three 2026 essays: build capacity before the disruption

Rutger Bregman · June 2026

Don’t abandon the field

“AI denial” is the left’s climate denial: “abandoning the field is not the same as stopping the technology.” A lab’s restraint is no substitute for public institutions: “conscience is not a policy”[51].

Bill Gates · Aug. 26, 2026

We are not preparing

The transition “will be one of the most turbulent times in human history … Right now, we are not preparing for it.” He proposes “Human Reserved” jobs and taxing robots like hiring[52].

Dario Amodei · Sept. 2026

Pace, don’t pause

“We must slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models,” with outside evaluators embedded at the lab, free to publish[53].

All three reject “shut it down”, and all three ask for capacity to be built before the disruption arrives.

Guardrails are interface design

Make hallucination checkable

The objectionWhat is missingThe control
“It invents citations”No retrieval step at allThe agent must call a real index
“It makes up metadata”Open vocabulary, nothing to checkTerms must resolve in an ontology
“It varies run to run”Sampling with no output contractA JSON schema fixes the shape; the other controls check the content
“I cannot audit it”No record of inputs or stepsProvenance in DuckLake; replay the tool calls

Each control was demonstrated with code and data in the Nov. 4 colloquium’s evidence repository[54].

The MESA pattern

Docs teach the agent how; tools fetch the data

1 · Speak

A researcher dictates the question and its constraints.

→

2 · Read

The agent reads llms.txt and learns which servers to install.

→

3 · Connect

MCP’s tools/list returns the live, authoritative tool catalogue.

→

4 · Query

Queries run where the data lives: read-only anonymously, with your rights once you sign in.

→

5 · Record

Each metadata write through mesa-mcp becomes a change record with provenance.

“If what you actually want is CyVerse data … do not scrape these pages: connect the servers and call their tools.”

MESA documentation, For AI agents[64]

CARC · UNM · CS 491/591 Intro to HCI · Nov. 13, 2026
Data lakehouse

A lakehouse that remembers

Lakehouse: cheap, directly accessible storage plus database features: safe concurrent updates (ACID transactions), versioning, auditing[65].

DuckLake: metadata in an ordinary SQL database, data in open Parquet files[66]; 1.0 in April 2026[67].

In MESA: every metadata-tag write through mesa-mcp (an iRODS attribute-value-unit, or AVU) is an append-only change record in DuckLake snapshots, so an agent can ask what a collection’s metadata was as of last Tuesday[68,69].

Ships today: AVU metadata history in DuckLake. Planned under the award, 2026–2029: the full lakehouse and a federated iRODS data mesh[70]. Figure: MESA proposal.

Resources you can use

What CARC offers students and faculty

GPUs and clusters

Easley: 8 NVIDIA H100 and 36 L40S GPUs. Hopper: 26 A100 and 2 V100[71]. The H100 and L40S partitions need an allocation your PI requests[72].

Free access

Free to UNM researchers: create an account, and a PI adds you to a project in ColdFront[73]. No regulated data (HIPAA, FERPA, CUI) on CARC systems[72].

People

Tickets at support.alliance.unm.edu, email help@carc.unm.edu, office hours and consultations[74].

Training

Semester workshops, domain workshops and course guest lectures[75]; open lessons on AI ethics in DUST 2026[61] and GPT 101[76].

Docs for agents

carc.unm.edu/docs/llms.txt, Markdown twins and a full corpus, with a human fallback[63].

Hosted AI: not yet

CARC “does not currently provide hosted AI, large language model (LLM), or agent services as a production service”; it points to the NAIRR Pilot, ACCESS and CyVerse AI-VERDE[77].

Take-aways for HCI · when the interface disappears

Design for the gulf of evaluation

01

Design for two readers

Publish llms.txt, Markdown twins and frontmatter next to the HTML.

02

Make checking cheap

Tests, validators, provenance and trust signals, so checking costs less than redoing.

03

Keep a human in reach

Disclose the AI, explain it, and give people a path to a person, as the Blueprint asks.

04

Engage, with care

Opting out is also a choice. Learn the tools with CARC’s free resources.

The question is becoming the interface to data. Design the data’s description, the prompt and the check together.

Backup

Going deeper: HCI principles for agents, three slides from the Agentic AI Loops lecture, MESA in more depth, and two activities for the class.
Three UI paradigms

From commands to outcomes

From about 1945

Batch

Hand over the whole job, come back for the printout. No interaction at all.

From about 1964

Command-based

Take turns, one command at a time. Command lines and graphical interfaces both live here. Nielsen files direct manipulation[79] here too, though its inventors framed it as a step beyond commands.

Now

Intent-based outcome specification

Say the result you want, not the steps. It “completely reverses the locus of control.”

Nielsen calls the third the first new UI paradigm in 60 years[80]. Vibe coding is intent-based interaction aimed at software.

CARC · UNM · CS 491/591 Intro to HCI · Nov. 13, 2026
The 1997 bet

The 1997 bet

“Direct manipulation interfaces are seen as more likely candidates to influence advanced user interfaces than adaptive, autonomous, intelligent agents. User control and responsibility are highly desirable.”

Ben Shneiderman, 1997[81]

Agents have arrived in the interface. His second sentence is still the design problem.

Plain-language definitions

Model, agent, harness, protocol

The model

A language model answers from what it read in training. It cannot see your files or run your code.

The agent

A loop around the model: read the goal, call a tool, read the result, decide the next call.

The harness

The program you actually run, such as Claude Code or Codex. It owns the loop, the files it may touch and the permissions.

The protocol

MCP, open since Nov. 2024[82]. Its docs call it “a USB-C port for AI applications”[83]: build a server once, and any agent that speaks MCP can use it.

CARC · UNM · CS 491/591 Intro to HCI · Nov. 13, 2026
A dial, not a switch

Vibe the prototype; engineer what others depend on

Vibe coding: accept every diffAgentic engineering: orchestrate, review, test
Simon Willison · Mar. 2025

“If an LLM wrote the code for you, and you then reviewed it, tested it thoroughly and made sure you could explain how it works to someone else that’s not vibe coding, it’s software development.”[84]

Karpathy · Feb. 2026

His new favorite name, “agentic engineering”: “you are not writing the code directly 99% of the time, you are orchestrating agents who do and acting as oversight.”[85]

Sarkar & Drosos · PPIG 2025

What the authors call the first empirical study of vibe coding, from 8+ hours of think-aloud video: expertise is not eliminated but moves to “context management, rapid code evaluation,” and knowing when to take over by hand[86].

How we keep vibe-coded repositories honest

Constraints and feedback, written for the agent

Contract

AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md say what the agent may edit, which files a script owns, and what it must never write[87].

Constraints

Closed vocabularies: fourteen page types, and ontology terms looked up in the Ontology Lookup Service, with a curator approving any mapping.

Feedback

Every push runs the validators: format conformance, a course lint, a strict build. The agent reads the errors and fixes them.

Evidence

Every number on my last talk’s slides has an evidence entry: code to rerun, data to trace, and a status, including “not yet checked”[54].

Norman’s design principles still apply. The user is now an agent: it is handed the manual every session, and the validators check whether it followed it.

CARC · UNM · CS 491/591 Intro to HCI · Nov. 13, 2026
Why speak a prompt?

Speaking beat thumb-typing about 3× when copying short phrases

2.9×

English speech vs. a phone keyboard, copying given phrases: 153 vs. 52 words per minute

Fewer errors while entering, slightly more left in the final text. A lab transcription task on phones, not composition; nobody has yet measured prompts to coding agents[88].

The articulation barrier

Prompting asks people to be “highly articulate” in written prose[89]. Speaking “probably alleviates the articulation barrier somewhat”[90].

Access, not convenience

For programmers with motor impairments, voice is the way in. They want to speak code naturally, not memorize unnatural command grammars[91].

Human-AI interaction

Old principles for new agents

PrincipleIn a coding agent
“Make clear what the system can do” (G1)[93]The harness shows the person the agent’s tools and permissions before it acts
“Make clear how well the system can do what it can do” (G2)[93]Status, sources and the verified tier in every page’s frontmatter
“Support efficient correction” (G9)[93]Small diffs, one commit per step, plan before edit, easy revert
Employ dialog to resolve key uncertainties[94]The agent asks before acting on an ambiguous request, weighing the cost of interrupting
Rapid, incremental, reversible operations[81]Git history for code; append-only DuckLake snapshots for metadata
Acceleration vs. exploration[95]Know which mode you are in: you know the next step, or you are asking the agent to show you options

From the Agentic AI Loops lecture

Who decides what happens next

Building blockIn ordinary softwareIn an AI agent
SequenceA programmer wrote the steps, in orderThe AI makes up the steps as it goes
SelectionA programmer wrote every if and else, and anyone can read and test themThe AI chooses, by reading descriptions written in plain English
IterationA programmer wrote the rule for when to stopThe AI decides when it is done, unless a step limit cuts it off

The three building blocks are still there. Their author is now an AI, deciding one step at a time[96].

AI sandboxes: fences for agents

Kind of fenceWhat it doesExamples
A sealed-off computerThe agent works inside a separate machine, so mistakes stay inside itVirtual machines, containers
Built-in limitsThe agent runs on your computer but may touch only certain files, commands and websitesPermission settings in Claude Code[97], Codex, Gemini CLI
Both at onceThe agent’s own limits, inside a sealed-off machineKubernetes pods with traffic through a proxy

Six habits: start with few permissions, review before running, use a dedicated environment, limit file access, watch what it does, keep backups[76].

Agentic AI

The agentic flow, as designed

Ask in plain language; the agent finds the data, runs the analysis, and returns a result you can audit.

In the colloquium’s evidence this flow ran over real MCP with a scripted plan standing in for the model, and keyword search standing in for retrieval[54]. Figure: MESA proposal.

CARC · UNM · CS 491/591 Intro to HCI · Nov. 13, 2026
A design pattern for the data layer

Give the agent its own account

Read rights only

An agent with its own iRODS account and read access cannot delete, overwrite or change permissions, whatever its intent.

Checked before it runs

iRODS policy enforcement points can stop an operation before it executes: who is asking, what rights they hold, which zone and path.

Owners keep control

The owner edits, moves, deletes and shares. Federated zones share data but keep their own catalogs and rules.

A pattern, not what every MESA agent does today: in Demo 1, the agent acts as the signed-in researcher, with that person’s rights[54].

CARC · UNM · CS 491/591 Intro to HCI · Nov. 13, 2026
Ontologies as guardrails

Terms resolve, or go to a curator

FieldWhat free text producesThe ontology term
Taxonground beetle · carabid · CarabidaeNCBITaxon:41073 Carabidae
Lengthmm · millimeters · millim.UO:0000016 millimetre
Areamm² · sq mm · mm2UO:0000082 square millimetre
Specimenpinned beetle · voucher · sampleOBI:0100051 specimen, by curator-approved mapping

Exact names and synonyms resolve through the Ontology Lookup Service. “carabid”, “millim.” and “sq mm” do not, so a person approves the mapping.

CARC · UNM · CS 491/591 Intro to HCI · Nov. 13, 2026
The stack

Five layers, each swappable by design

Open source where it exists (Kubernetes, DuckLake, iRODS, Lustre); some backends, such as VAST and AWS S3, are proprietary. Running today on CyVerse; TACC, Jetstream2 and OSN are planned. Figure: MESA proposal.

claude mcp add \
  --transport http formation \

Sign in with CyVerse in the browser, then ask in plain language: list my running apps; list the folders in my collection.

CARC · UNM · CS 491/591 Intro to HCI · Nov. 13, 2026
Activity · 10 minutes · pairs

Try it: dictate a brief

1

Pick a task

A small change to something you built this term.

2

Type it

Write the prompt as you normally would. Count the words.

3

Say it

Dictate it with your phone or laptop’s built-in dictation, for one minute. Count again.

4

Compare

What did speech add: goal, context, constraints, how to check? What did it get wrong?

Discuss: which gulf did each version help with, execution or evaluation?

CARC · UNM · CS 491/591 Intro to HCI · Nov. 13, 2026
Activity · 15 minutes · groups

Try it: design for the second reader

Choose a site

A site you use every week: a department page, a course site, a library guide.

Write its llms.txt

One summary paragraph, then five links with one-line descriptions. What would an agent need first?

Add trust signals

For each link: what type of page, who wrote it, when it goes stale, and who checked it.

Discuss: what does a human reader lose or gain from the same signals?
